Develop each distinct individual once

Source: R/develop_unique.R
develop_unique.Rd

Wraps a development function so that individuals with the same key are developed only once and share the result. This saves time when many new individuals share a genotype, as with discrete allelic values (few alleles per locus, recombined in sexual populations). With continuous mutational effects nearly every genotype is distinct, and it only adds overhead.

Usage

develop_unique(dev, key = dev_key_exact)

Arguments

dev

A function `dev(G, X0)` of a genotype matrix and a matrix of starting expression states, one row per individual.

key

A function `key(G, X0)` returning one string per individual. Individuals with equal keys must develop identically. See [dev_key_exact()] and [dev_key_genotype()].

Value

A function with the same interface as `dev`.

Details

The wrapper is independent of the simulation loop. It applies to any function `dev(G, X0)` that returns a list whose elements have one row (or one entry) per individual, as [develop()] does (`X`, `status`). Other kinds of individuals, for example several motifs in one population, need a `key` that tells them apart (e.g. a motif id), or no de-duplication.

See also

[simulate_population()] (argument `dedupe`).
